code_evidence.observation: In BpmnUpdater.prototype.updateDiParent, (parentDi || di.$parent).get('planeElement') is called; when di.$parent is undefined and parentDi is falsy (e.g. during removal/re-parenting of shapes outside a container or pool), accessing .get on undefined throws Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get').

hypotheses: When replacing/morphing a DataStoreReference into a DataObjectReference outside of a pool, parentDi and/or di.$parent may be undefined during removal or parent updating, causing `(parentDi || di.$parent).get('planeElement')` in `updateDiParent` to throw a TypeError.
Alternatively or additionally, DataObjectReferences may be constrained by modeling rules regarding whether they are allowed to exist directly on a collaboration root outside of a pool/process.

refined_predictions.symptom: An uncaught TypeError is thrown in the console when a DataStoreReference located outside of a pool is morphed into a DataObjectReference.
refined_predictions.expected_behavior: One of: Don't allow to morph to DataObjectReference outside of Pool, or Allow morph, but don't break.

observations.detail: A DataStoreReference icon is located outside the pool on the canvas and selected.
The replace/morph menu option 'Data Object Reference' is clicked.
A red uncaught TypeError stack trace appears in the browser console.

refined_predictions.uncertainty: Whether the desired solution is to restrict replace options in the menu outside of pools or to ensure updateDiParent handles or resolves the missing DI plane gracefully without throwing.

questions: Should DataObjectReferences be disallowed from existing outside of a pool in collaborations (e.g. via rules/ReplaceMenuProvider), or should morphing be permitted by properly resolving or guarding the DI parent/planeElement?

code_evidence.observation: LabelEditingProvider cancels or completes direct editing on events like 'commandStack.changed', 'canvas.viewbox.changing', etc., but does not listen for root/plane change events (such as 'root.set').

hypotheses: When switching planes (e.g. via breadcrumbs or drilldown navigation triggering root.set), the directEditing instance is not canceled or completed, leaving the active editing overlay mounted on the canvas.

refined_predictions.symptom: When switching planes with direct editing active on an element inside a sub-process, the direct editing box or overlay remains open after navigation.
refined_predictions.expected_behavior: Direct editing is canceled on plane switch.

observations.detail: User drills down into collapsed sub-process 'choose recipe' and direct edits an element.
User clicks 'Process_1' breadcrumb link to navigate back to parent plane.
Parent plane is displayed with collapsed sub-process, but an orphaned direct editing input box remains visible on the canvas.

refined_predictions.uncertainty: Whether switching planes should cancel or complete direct editing.

questions: Should direct editing be canceled (discarding uncommitted edits) or completed (committing current text) when switching planes / root elements?

code_evidence.observation: DrilldownOverlayBehavior only populates drilldown overlays on 'import.done' and reacts to shape toggleCollapse / shape create / shape move / shape delete commands, but does not listen to canvas root changes (e.g. root.set) or re-attach overlays when switching between different planes/diagrams

hypotheses: Drilldown overlays are attached to elements upon initial import or shape commands, but when external diagram navigation or canvas root switching occurs (such as via multi-diagram plugins or switching root planes), overlays attached to elements on previous planes may be cleared or not restored upon returning to root.

refined_predictions.symptom: The deep linking overlay for the subprocess is lost after navigating between diagrams using the multi-diagram plugin.
refined_predictions.expected_behavior: The deep linking overlay button on collapsed subprocess elements should remain visible or be restored when navigating between diagrams/roots.

observations.detail: At t=0.625s to 1.875s, the subprocess element has a visible blue drilldown overlay button in the root diagram.
At t=3.125s, clicking the drilldown overlay switches the canvas view into the subprocess (Activity_019fqik).
At t=6.25s, navigating back to Root via breadcrumbs shows the drilldown overlay still present.
At t=13.75s to 16.538s, opening the multi-diagram menu and navigating between diagrams causes the drilldown overlay to be missing when returning to Root.

refined_predictions.uncertainty: It is uncertain whether the loss of overlay is triggered specifically by the third-party multi-diagram plugin's diagram replacement or by missing root-change event handlers in bpmn-js drilldown.

questions: Should drilldown overlays be managed and restored dynamically on canvas root changes ('root.set') across multiple root elements or multi-diagram switches?
Does bpmn-js officially support third-party multi-diagram plugins switching roots directly, or is drilldown expected to handle arbitrary rootElement switching?

code_evidence.observation: In ensureInternalLabelDi, when !text && di.label, di.label is assigned null (`di.label = null;`) instead of deleting or unsetting the property or setting it to undefined/removing it from the DI object.

hypotheses: Setting di.label = null in UpdateLabelHandler.js leaves the label property present with a null value on the DI model object, causing downstream consumers and linters expecting di.label to be either an object or undefined to fail with TypeErrors (e.g., reading properties of null). Removing the property (e.g. delete di.label or setting di.label = undefined) when text is empty may be needed.

refined_predictions.symptom: When a task's label is removed, its di object retains a label property with a null value instead of removing the property entirely.

observations.detail: User double clicks task 'a', clears the label text, and clicks outside to commit the empty label.
Linting integration runs immediately after label removal and logs multiple rule failures in the console.
Console displays TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '$instanceOf') originating from linter traversing di.label.

refined_predictions.uncertainty: Whether di.label should be deleted or set to undefined according to moddle schema expectations.

questions: Should clearing internal labels delete the `label` property entirely from `di` (or set it to `undefined`), and are there any moddle / command stack undo-redo semantics or other handlers (such as BpmnUpdater or LabelBehavior) that also need to align with this behavior?

hypotheses: When toggling between parallel and sequential multi-instance (both represented by bpmn:MultiInstanceLoopCharacteristics), ReplaceMenuProvider creates a fresh moddle element instead of updating or retaining the existing MultiInstanceLoopCharacteristics object's existing properties/children and merely toggling isSequential.

refined_predictions.symptom: When changing a sub-process's multi-instance setting from parallel to sequential, configured multi-instance properties (such as loop cardinality and completion condition) are lost.

observations.detail: SubProcess has parallel multi-instance with Loop Cardinality '1' and Completion Condition '${foo}'. User opens the replace popup menu.
User selects 'Sequential Multi Instance' in the popup menu.

SubProcess marker changes to sequential multi-instance, but properties panel Multi Instance fields (Loop Cardinality, Completion Condition) are cleared and a validation error appears ('Must provide either loop cardinality or collection').

hypotheses: In SetColorHandler.prototype.postExecute, when updating moddle properties for an element with labelTarget, the label's color property is assigned di['background-color'] (the fill color) rather than di['border-color'] (the stroke color).

code_evidence.observation: LayoutConnectionBehavior intercepts 'connection.layout' and 'connection.updateWaypoints' to adjust endpoints for incoming and outgoing connections (such as associations), but does not reposition labels (connection.label or connection.labels) when connection waypoints change.

hypotheses: When a connected shape is resized or a connection is re-laid out (triggering connection.layout / connection.updateWaypoints), LayoutConnectionBehavior updates connection anchor points for associations but does not reposition the connection's own label(s) or adjust associations when hints/waypoints change under certain layout conditions.

refined_predictions.symptom: When a Sub Process shape is resized or its connected connection is re-laid out, the connected sequence flow label and text association fail to reposition correctly along with the connection/shape and remain detached or hanging in place.
refined_predictions.expected_behavior: Label and Association are moved with it

observations.detail: Initial diagram shows Sub Process 1 connected to End Event with sequence flow, bendpoint, and text annotation/label positioned near the flow line.
Sub Process 1 bottom edge is resized/dragged down (around t=5.6s - 6.5s), causing the sequence flow to re-route straight horizontally from the middle of Sub Process 1 to End Event.
The label 'LAbel' and the text annotation remain stranded downwards / disconnected from the newly routed straight sequence flow line.

refined_predictions.uncertainty: LayoutConnectionBehavior currently handles associations on connection.layout and connection.updateWaypoints, but does not move connection labels, and association anchor recalculation may not handle all layout recalculations during shape resizing.

questions: Should connection labels be automatically updated/re-anchored inside LayoutConnectionBehavior or via a dedicated label layout/reconnection behavior?
When the sequence flow is re-routed drastically due to shape resizing, should the text annotation association re-anchor to the closest segment or preserve relative waypoint distance?
